correctness.rationale: The recent source's primary abstract states the exact characterization of segment-multiplier boundedness by the large-scale Muckenhoupt condition obtained by restricting the usual \(A_p\) test to intervals of length at least one. For the submitted weight, the reciprocal is \(|x|^{-1}(\log(e/|x|))^{-\gamma/(p-1)}\); the substitution \(u=\log(e/x)\) makes its compact-defect mass \(\int_1^\infty u^{-q}du\), finite exactly for \(q>1\), hence \(\gamma>p-1\). Because both factors equal one outside the defect, that integrability is also sufficient for all large intervals. The classical small-interval product and the blow-up of the truncated characteristic follow from the same exact reciprocal integral and standard endpoint integration.

final_claim: For the patched critical power-log weight \(w_\gamma(x)=|x|^{p-1}(\log(e/|x|))^\gamma\) on \(0<|x|<1\) and \(1\) outside, the segment multiplier is bounded on \(L^p(w_\gamma)\) exactly when \(\gamma>p-1\); the weight never lies in classical \(A_p\), and the submitted small-scale and truncated-characteristic asymptotics hold.
